claim: Dinitrogen reduction in the biological nitrogen cycle is catalyzed by nitrogenase, a two-component metalloenzyme.
source: Dinitrogen reduction in the biological nitrogen cycle is catalyzed by nitrogenase, a two-component metalloenzyme.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about nitrogenase function.

claim: Selenocyanate is a newly identified substrate and inhibitor of nitrogenase.
source: Here we report the catalysis dependent, site-selective incorporation of selenium into the FeMo-cofactor from selenocyanate as a newly identified substrate and inhibitor.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the manuscript based on experimental work.

claim: The structure of Se2B-labeled MoFe-protein was determined at 1.60 Å resolution.
source: The 1.60 Å resolution structure reveals selenium occupying the S2B site of FeMo-cofactor in the Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe-protein, a position that was recently identified as the CO-binding site.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental data regarding crystal structure resolution.

claim: Selenium occupies the S2B site of FeMo-cofactor in the Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe-protein.
source: The 1.60 Å resolution structure reveals selenium occupying the S2B site of FeMo-cofactor in the Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe-protein, a position that was recently identified as the CO-binding site.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data and shown in Figure 1A, B, C.

claim: The S2B position was recently identified as the CO-binding site.
source: The 1.60 Å resolution structure reveals selenium occupying the S2B site of FeMo-cofactor in the Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe-protein, a position that was recently identified as the CO-binding site.
evidence: This refers to previous work, likely by the same authors.

claim: The Se2B-labeled enzyme retains substrate reduction activity.
source: The Se2B-labeled enzyme retains substrate reduction activity and marks the starting point for a crystallographic pulse-chase experiment of the active site during turnover.
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: All three belt-sulfur sites of the FeMo-cofactor are exchangeable.
source: Through a series of crystal structures obtained at resolutions of 1.32–1.66 Å, including the CO-inhibited form of Av1-Se2B, the exchangeability of all three belt-sulfur sites is demonstrated, providing direct insights into unforeseen rearrangements of the metal center during catalysis.
evidence: This is demonstrated through multiple crystal structures at different time points shown in Figure 2.

claim: The reduction of substrates by nitrogenase entails multiple cycles of association and dissociation between two component proteins for sequential transfer of electrons.
source: The reduction of substrates by nitrogenase entails multiple cycles of association and dissociation between two component proteins for sequential transfer of electrons (Burgess and Lowe, 1996; Howard and Rees, 2006; Hoffman et al., 2014; Hageman and Burris, 1978).
evidence: This is supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Electrons are transferred from the [4Fe:4S]-cluster of the homodimeric Fe-protein to the MoFe-protein in a reaction requiring adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis.
source: In the transient complex, electrons are transferred from the [4Fe:4S]-cluster of the homodimeric Fe-protein to the MoFe-protein in a reaction requiring adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis (Burgess and Lowe, 1996; Howard and Rees, 1994).
evidence: This is supported by literature citations.

claim: The MoFe-protein is an (αβ)2 tetramer.
source: The MoFe-protein, an (αβ)2 tetramer, contains two types of unique metal centers per catalytic αβ-unit: the P-cluster [8Fe:7S] and the FeMo-cofactor [7Fe:9S:C:Mo]-R-homocitrate (Kim and Rees, 1992; Einsle et al., 2002; Spatzal et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The MoFe-protein contains two types of unique metal centers per catalytic αβ-unit: the P-cluster [8Fe:7S] and the FeMo-cofactor [7Fe:9S:C:Mo]-R-homocitrate.
source: The MoFe-protein, an (αβ)2 tetramer, contains two types of unique metal centers per catalytic αβ-unit: the P-cluster [8Fe:7S] and the FeMo-cofactor [7Fe:9S:C:Mo]-R-homocitrate (Kim and Rees, 1992; Einsle et al., 2002; Spatzal et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The P-cluster is the initial electron acceptor with subsequent transfer to the FeMo-cofactor.
source: The P-cluster is the initial electron acceptor with subsequent transfer to the FeMo-cofactor, one of the most elaborate metalloclusters found in nature and the catalytic center of biological nitrogen reduction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the electron transfer pathway in nitrogenase.

claim: The FeMo-cofactor is one of the most elaborate metalloclusters found in nature and the catalytic center of biological nitrogen reduction.
source: The P-cluster is the initial electron acceptor with subsequent transfer to the FeMo-cofactor, one of the most elaborate metalloclusters found in nature and the catalytic center of biological nitrogen reduction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the FeMo-cofactor.

claim: For substrates and inhibitors to bind, the FeMo-cofactor resting state must be reduced by two to four electrons provided by the Fe-protein.
source: For substrates and inhibitors to bind, the FeMo-cofactor resting state must be reduced by two to four electrons provided by the Fe-protein (Burgess and Lowe, 1996; Thorneley and Lowe, 1985).
evidence: This is supported by literature citations.

claim: The characterization of bound species including reaction intermediates has proven to be experimentally challenging due to the transitory nature of these states.
source: The characterization of bound species including reaction intermediates has proven to be experimentally challenging due to the transitory nature of these states, inevitably leading to a recovery of the FeMo-cofactor resting state.
evidence: This is a general statement about experimental challenges in the field.

claim: The crystal structure of Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe-protein with the inhibitor CO has provided high resolution details of a bound ligand.
source: While a number of studies have investigated substrate and inhibitor interactions (Lee et al., 1997; George et al., 1997; Pickett et al., 2004; Seefeldt et al., 2004; Davis et al., 1979), only the recent crystal structure of Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe-protein (Av1) with the inhibitor CO (Av1-CO) has provided high resolution details of a bound ligand (Spatzal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The high symmetry and complex electronic structure of the FeMo-cofactor complicate spectroscopic studies.
source: In addition, the high symmetry and complex electronic structure of the FeMo-cofactor complicate spectroscopic studies (Spatzal, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The S2B position of the active site can be reversibly replaced with CO.
source: Because the S2B position of the active site can be reversibly replaced with CO (Spatzal et al., 2014), it represents a potential site for other substitutions by substrates and inhibitors.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Se is a structural surrogate for S in [Fe:S] clusters.
source: Se, a structural surrogate for S in [Fe:S] clusters (Meyer et al., 1992; Zheng et al., 2012), has crystallographic and spectroscopic properties that make it an excellent probe, hence, potential Se containing compounds were investigated.
evidence: This is supported by literature citations.

claim: Thiocyanate (SCN-) is both a substrate and an inhibitor of nitrogenase.
source: Based upon the previous recognition, that thiocyanate (SCN-) is both a substrate and an inhibitor of nitrogenase (Rasche and Seefeldt, 1997), we evaluated the kinetic properties of selenocyanate (SeCN-).
evidence: This is supported by a literature citation.

claim: SeCN- has a pKa < 1.
source: We found SeCN- (pKa < 1 [Boughton and Keller, 1966]) to be a poor substrate as measured by methane production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), a product also observed in thiocyanate (Rasche and Seefeldt, 1997) and cyanide (Li et al., 1982) reduction.
evidence: This is supported by a literature citation.

claim: SeCN- is a poor substrate as measured by methane production.
source: We found SeCN- (pKa < 1 [Boughton and Keller, 1966]) to be a poor substrate as measured by methane production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), a product also observed in thiocyanate (Rasche and Seefeldt, 1997) and cyanide (Li et al., 1982) reduction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Methane is a product observed in thiocyanate reduction.
source: We found SeCN- (pKa < 1 [Boughton and Keller, 1966]) to be a poor substrate as measured by methane production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), a product also observed in thiocyanate (Rasche and Seefeldt, 1997) and cyanide (Li et al., 1982) reduction.
evidence: This is supported by a literature citation.

claim: Methane is a product observed in cyanide reduction.
source: We found SeCN- (pKa < 1 [Boughton and Keller, 1966]) to be a poor substrate as measured by methane production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), a product also observed in thiocyanate (Rasche and Seefeldt, 1997) and cyanide (Li et al., 1982) reduction.
evidence: This is supported by a literature citation.

claim: SeCN- is a potent, yet reversible inhibitor of acetylene reduction.
source: In addition, SeCN- is a potent, yet reversible inhibitor of acetylene reduction with an inhibition constant 30 times lower than observed for SCN- (Ki (SeCN-) = 410 ± 30 μM versus Ki (SCN-) = 12.7 ± 1.2 mM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The inhibition constant of SeCN- is 410 ± 30 μM.
source: In addition, SeCN- is a potent, yet reversible inhibitor of acetylene reduction with an inhibition constant 30 times lower than observed for SCN- (Ki (SeCN-) = 410 ± 30 μM versus Ki (SCN-) = 12.7 ± 1.2 mM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from inhibition assays.

claim: The inhibition constant of SCN- is 12.7 ± 1.2 mM.
source: In addition, SeCN- is a potent, yet reversible inhibitor of acetylene reduction with an inhibition constant 30 times lower than observed for SCN- (Ki (SeCN-) = 410 ± 30 μM versus Ki (SCN-) = 12.7 ± 1.2 mM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from inhibition assays.

claim: The inhibition constant of SeCN- is 30 times lower than that of SCN-.
source: In addition, SeCN- is a potent, yet reversible inhibitor of acetylene reduction with an inhibition constant 30 times lower than observed for SCN- (Ki (SeCN-) = 410 ± 30 μM versus Ki (SCN-) = 12.7 ± 1.2 mM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is calculated from the experimental Ki values.

claim: Proton reduction activity is retained in the presence of SeCN-, although at a decreased level.
source: In contrast to inhibition of acetylene reduction, proton reduction activity is retained, although at a decreased level (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Se from SeCN- could be incorporated into the FeMo-cofactor by incubating nitrogenase under assay (turnover) conditions with concentrations of SeCN- sufficient to inhibit acetylene reduction.
source: By screening a range of experimental parameters, we found that Se from SeCN- could be incorporated into the FeMo-cofactor by incubating nitrogenase under assay (turnover) conditions with concentrations of SeCN- sufficient to inhibit acetylene reduction.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method and findings.

claim: Se quantitatively replaced belt-S position S2B in the FeMo-cofactor.
source: The 1.60 Å resolution crystal structure of Av1 (Av1-Se2B), isolated from assays containing SeCN- (Figure 1A, B, C), revealed that Se quantitatively replaced belt-S position S2B in the FeMo-cofactor thereby generating the [7Fe:8S:1Se:Mo:C]-R-homocitrate cluster (FeMoSe-cofactor) form of the MoFe-protein.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The essentially exclusive substitution of S2B by Se was validated by anomalous difference Fourier maps calculated from data measured at the Se-K edge f''-peak position of 12,662 eV.
source: The essentially exclusive substitution of S2B by Se was validated by anomalous difference Fourier maps calculated from data measured at the Se-K edge f''-peak position of 12,662 eV (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: At 1.60 Å resolution, no perturbation of the cofactor structure or its environment was detected.
source: At this resolution, no perturbation of the cofactor structure or its environment was detected, reflecting the small increase (3.8%) in the ionic radius of Se relative to S (Zheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data and comparison with literature.

claim: The ionic radius of Se is 3.8% larger than that of S.
source: At this resolution, no perturbation of the cofactor structure or its environment was detected, reflecting the small increase (3.8%) in the ionic radius of Se relative to S (Zheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a literature citation.

claim: A low occupancy Se site (ranging from 0–20% under different conditions) was identified adjacent to a previously identified potential sulfur-binding site located ~22 Å away from the FeMo-cofactor at the interface of the α and β subunits.
source: Except for a low occupancy site (ranging from 0–20% under different conditions) adjacent to the previously identified potential sulfur-binding site (located ~22 Å away from the FeMo-cofactor at the interface of the α and β subunits [Spatzal et al., 2014]), no other Se sites were identified in the anomalous difference Fourier map.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data and references previous work.

claim: Av1-Se2B retains acetylene and dinitrogen reduction activity when compared to native Av1.
source: Significantly, Av1-Se2B retains acetylene and dinitrogen reduction activity when compared to native Av1 (Figure 1D,E), with the difference that the activity time course for Av1-Se2B with acetylene and dinitrogen exhibits a longer initial lag phase than for native Av1 (Figure 1D inset, E).
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The activity time course for Av1-Se2B with acetylene and dinitrogen exhibits a longer initial lag phase than for native Av1.
source: Significantly, Av1-Se2B retains acetylene and dinitrogen reduction activity when compared to native Av1 (Figure 1D,E), with the difference that the activity time course for Av1-Se2B with acetylene and dinitrogen exhibits a longer initial lag phase than for native Av1 (Figure 1D inset, E).
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Crystal structures of the enzyme were determined at seven time points after initiation of substrate turnover corresponding to 2 to 5360 acetylene reduced per active site.
source: Crystal structures of the enzyme were determined at seven time points after initiation of substrate turnover corresponding to 2 to 5360 acetylene reduced per active site.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach and data collection.

claim: The structures designated Av1-Se-fq-2 to Av1-Se-fq-5360 were determined at resolutions of 1.32–1.66 Å.
source: These structures (designated Av1-Se-fq-2 to Av1-Se-fq-5360), at resolutions of 1.32–1.66 Å, represent the first example of time-dependent structural snapshots of the nitrogenase active site during turnover (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This describes the crystallographic data obtained.

claim: These structures represent the first example of time-dependent structural snapshots of the nitrogenase active site during turnover.
source: These structures (designated Av1-Se-fq-2 to Av1-Se-fq-5360), at resolutions of 1.32–1.66 Å, represent the first example of time-dependent structural snapshots of the nitrogenase active site during turnover (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the experimental approach.

claim: There is a correlation between enzyme catalysis and the migration of Se from its initial Se2B site into the two remaining belt sulfur positions (S5A and S3A).
source: The time course series of crystallographic data demonstrates a correlation between enzyme catalysis and the migration of Se from its initial Se2B site into the two remaining belt sulfur positions (S5A and S3A).
evidence: This is supported by the time-resolved crystallographic data shown in Figure 2.

claim: All belt-S atoms of FeMo-cofactor, separated by 5.7 Å in the resting state, can interchange during substrate (acetylene) reduction.
source: Consequently all belt-S atoms of FeMo-cofactor, separated by 5.7 Å in the resting state, can interchange during substrate (acetylene) reduction (Figure 2, Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the crystallographic data shown in Figure 2 and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: The Se migration from S2B favors S5A over S3A at the earliest time points.
source: The Se migration from S2B favors S5A over S3A at the earliest time points (Figure 2, Supplementary file 1A), but whether this reflects an ordered sequence or a more complex mechanism cannot be established from these data.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data shown in Figure 2 and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: With a sufficient number of catalytic turnovers (several thousand), the total Se is lost and apparently replaced by S, leading to a recovery of the original FeMo-cofactor.
source: Remarkably, with a sufficient number of catalytic turnovers (several thousand, Figure 2A), the total Se is lost and apparently replaced by S, leading to a recovery of the original FeMo-cofactor (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Neither the source of S nor the pathway(s) by which Se exits the MoFe-protein have been identified.
source: Neither the source of this S, nor the pathway(s) by which Se exits the MoFe-protein, have been identified.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about the limitations of the current findings.

claim: All three belt-positions are labilized during the reduction of acetylene.
source: The observation that Se2B can migrate to S5A and S3A and is ultimately chased from the cofactor, clearly implies that all three belt-positions are labilized during the reduction of acetylene.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Se migration data.

claim: Little or no migration of Se2B was observed during proton reduction.
source: In contrast, little or no migration of Se2B was observed during proton reduction.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The Av1-Se-CO structure was determined at a resolution of 1.53 Å.
source: The Av1-Se-CO structure at a resolution of 1.53 Å revealed that Se2B was ca. 90% replaced by a bridging CO with a geometry nearly identical to that observed for Av1-CO (Figure 3) (Spatzal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is crystallographic data.

claim: In Av1-Se-CO, Se2B was ca. 90% replaced by a bridging CO with a geometry nearly identical to that observed for Av1-CO.
source: The Av1-Se-CO structure at a resolution of 1.53 Å revealed that Se2B was ca. 90% replaced by a bridging CO with a geometry nearly identical to that observed for Av1-CO (Figure 3) (Spatzal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 3 and comparison with previous work.

claim: In Av1-Se-CO, Se was not expelled from the FeMo-cofactor but migrated to the other two belt positions with ca. 88% overall retention.
source: Unexpectedly, Se was not expelled from the FeMo-cofactor but migrated to the other two belt positions with ca. 88% overall retention (Se occupancy: 10% (x2B; where x reflects a mixture of S and Se), 35% (x3A) and 44% (x5A)).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The catalytic state of the cofactor capable of interacting with CO is similar to that which reacts with substrates.
source: This result augments our findings from acetylene turnover, namely that the catalytic state of the cofactor capable of interacting with CO is similar to that which reacts with substrates.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the CO inhibition and acetylene turnover data.

claim: The path of net loss of sulfur from the cofactor is through either one or both of the other belt positions (not S2B).
source: In contrast to the simple model of CO displacement and loss of S from S2B previously envisioned (Spatzal et al., 2014), the path of net loss of sulfur from the cofactor is through either one or both of the other belt positions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Av1-Se-CO data, contrasting with previous models.

claim: The incorporation and migration of the site-specific reporter, Se, demonstrates unanticipated dynamics of cofactor elements.
source: The incorporation and migration of the site-specific reporter, Se, demonstrates unanticipated dynamics of cofactor elements, specifically that the belt sulfur atoms, S2B, S5A, and S3A, can interchange and exchange with exogenous ligands under turnover conditions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The belt sulfur atoms, S2B, S5A, and S3A, can interchange and exchange with exogenous ligands under turnover conditions.
source: The incorporation and migration of the site-specific reporter, Se, demonstrates unanticipated dynamics of cofactor elements, specifically that the belt sulfur atoms, S2B, S5A, and S3A, can interchange and exchange with exogenous ligands under turnover conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The lability of the S2B position towards ligand exchange in non-resting states of the FeMo-cofactor highlights the likely role for the Fe2-Fe6 edge as a primary interaction site for substrates and inhibitors.
source: The lability of the S2B position towards ligand exchange in non-resting states of the FeMo-cofactor highlights the likely role for the Fe2-Fe6 edge as a primary interaction site for substrates and inhibitors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Both CO and Se from SeCN-, with different chemical properties, are incorporated at the S2B site.
source: Both CO (Spatzal et al., 2014) and Se from SeCN-, with different chemical properties, are incorporated at this site.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from this study and previous work.

claim: The side-chain residues flanking the S2B position were previously identified to be catalytically important as demonstrated by mutagenesis studies.
source: Significantly, the side-chain residues flanking this position were previously identified to be catalytically important as demonstrated by mutagenesis studies (Benton et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a literature citation.

claim: The lack of substrate or inhibitor binding to the FeMo-cofactor resting state could be the result of the sulfurs serving as protecting groups that shield the iron core.
source: The lack of substrate or inhibitor binding to the FeMo-cofactor resting state could be the result of the sulfurs serving as protecting groups that shield the iron core (Howard and Rees, 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: The displacement of belt S in the catalytically active reduced states would effectively de-protect these Fe sites, thereby activating them for reaction with substrates.
source: The displacement of belt S in the catalytically active reduced states would effectively de-protect these Fe sites, thereby activating them for reaction with substrates.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic interpretation of the data.

claim: The interchange of all belt-S atoms is suggestive that substrates may also migrate to different sites of the trigonal six-iron prism during catalysis.
source: The interchange of all belt-S atoms is suggestive that substrates may also migrate to different sites of the trigonal six-iron prism during catalysis.
evidence: This is a speculative inference drawn from the Se migration data.

claim: The belt-S interchange may involve a twist-type mechanism interconverting trigonal prism and octahedral forms of the six-iron core.
source: While the underlying mechanism(s) are not known, one can speculate this may involve a twist-type mechanism interconverting trigonal prism and octahedral forms of the six-iron core, where swapping Fe-S bonding partners in the latter would result in interchange of the belt-S.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation about a possible mechanism.

claim: The resting state structure of FeMo-cofactor does not capture key features of the catalytic state.
source: Our results indicate that the resting state structure of FeMo-cofactor does not capture key features of the catalytic state, and a detailed understanding of how nitrogenase reduces dinitrogen must include the role of cofactor rearrangements during turnover.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: A detailed understanding of how nitrogenase reduces dinitrogen must include the role of cofactor rearrangements during turnover.
source: Our results indicate that the resting state structure of FeMo-cofactor does not capture key features of the catalytic state, and a detailed understanding of how nitrogenase reduces dinitrogen must include the role of cofactor rearrangements during turnover.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The incorporation of selenium into FeMo-cofactor opens a novel route to probe the substrate reduction mechanism of nitrogenase by using its unique crystallographic and spectroscopic properties.
source: Furthermore, the incorporation of selenium into FeMo-cofactor opens a novel route to probe the substrate reduction mechanism of nitrogenase by using its unique crystallographic and spectroscopic properties.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications and future applications of the findings.

claim: The specific activity of Av1 was 2350 ± 100 nmol min-1 mg-1 when measured by acetylene reduction at saturation of each component.
source: The specific activity of Av1 was 2350 ± 100 nmol min-1 mg-1and of Av2 was 2060 ± 55 nmol min-1 mg-1 when measured by acetylene reduction at saturation of each component.
evidence: This is experimental data from activity assays.

claim: The specific activity of Av2 was 2060 ± 55 nmol min-1 mg-1 when measured by acetylene reduction at saturation of each component.
source: The specific activity of Av1 was 2350 ± 100 nmol min-1 mg-1and of Av2 was 2060 ± 55 nmol min-1 mg-1 when measured by acetylene reduction at saturation of each component.
evidence: This is experimental data from activity assays.

claim: Incorporation of Se required full nitrogenase turnover as SeCN- incubation with Av1 alone was ineffective.
source: Significantly, incorporation of Se required full nitrogenase turnover as SeCN- incubation with Av1 alone was ineffective; likewise, the non-substrate Na2Se failed to serve as a Se donor even when incubated under turnover conditions.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The non-substrate Na2Se failed to serve as a Se donor even when incubated under turnover conditions.
source: Significantly, incorporation of Se required full nitrogenase turnover as SeCN- incubation with Av1 alone was ineffective; likewise, the non-substrate Na2Se failed to serve as a Se donor even when incubated under turnover conditions.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The standard deviation between anomalous density values for the Fe-atoms was ≤ 4%.
source: The standard deviation between anomalous density values for the Fe-atoms was ≤ 4%.
evidence: This is a statistical measure from the crystallographic analysis.

claim: The average B-factor for isotropically refined atoms in the Av1-Se2B structure is 9.3 ± 1 Å2.
source: No adjustments were made for variation in B factors since the Fe and S components of both metalloclusters have similar values (average and standard deviation = 9.3 ± 1 Å2 for isotropically refined B-factors in the Av1-Se2B structure).
evidence: This is crystallographic data.

claim: For Fe and S in the FeMo-cofactor, the B values are 9.0 ± 0.4 Å2.
source: For Fe and S in the FeMo-cofactor, the corresponding B values are 9.0 ± 0.4 Å2, with the B for Se2B = 9.9 ± 0.5 Å2 and the average B for the entire protein structure = 13.8 Å2.
evidence: This is crystallographic data.

claim: The B-factor for Se2B is 9.9 ± 0.5 Å2.
source: For Fe and S in the FeMo-cofactor, the corresponding B values are 9.0 ± 0.4 Å2, with the B for Se2B = 9.9 ± 0.5 Å2 and the average B for the entire protein structure = 13.8 Å2.
evidence: This is crystallographic data.

claim: The average B-factor for the entire protein structure is 13.8 Å2.
source: For Fe and S in the FeMo-cofactor, the corresponding B values are 9.0 ± 0.4 Å2, with the B for Se2B = 9.9 ± 0.5 Å2 and the average B for the entire protein structure = 13.8 Å2.
evidence: This is crystallographic data.

claim: The anomalous scattering of S is 6.3% that of Se at an energy of 12,662 eV.
source: Quantification of Se-occupancies was further improved by including the contribution of the residual anomalous density of sulfur, with the anomalous scattering of S being 6.3% that of Se (f''(S)/f''(Se)) at an energy of 12,662 eV.
evidence: This is based on known physical properties of the elements at the specified energy.

claim: The largest deviation between Se-anomalous densities observed for the two crystallographically independent copies of FeMo-cofactor was found to be ~5%.
source: The largest deviation between Se-anomalous densities observed for the two crystallographically independent copies of FeMo-cofactor was found to be ~5%, which provides an estimate of the uncertainty in the occupancy values.
evidence: This is a statistical measure from the crystallographic analysis.

claim: The root mean square value of the anomalous electron density map is ~2% of the Se peak value.
source: The root mean square value of the anomalous electron density map is ~2% of the Se peak value, which sets a lower threshold on the minimum occupancy that can be detected at this site.
evidence: This is a statistical measure from the crystallographic analysis.
